PR 2501 corrective verification

Project save

Baseline e3d0806d rejects a synthetic MVR 1.6 Fixture containing CastShadow and CustomCommands, after a Fixture name/transform edit and a Layout text edit. RecordStandardPreservationRisks retains both source subtrees, but CheckStandardPreservation rejects them before the archive can be completed. The baseline diagnostic is StandardDataPreservationBlocked / Error / ExportFailed at /GeneralSceneDescription/Scene/Layers/Layer/ChildList/Fixture/CastShadow and the corresponding CustomCommands path. This does not identify the cause of the user's private file failure.

The regression input is independently validated against the pinned official MVR 1.6 XSD. Both fields now survive normal project save, actual project reload, and a second save. The original source archive remains byte-identical. Embedded and standalone canonical MVR have identical ordered entry names and payloads. The test also inspects the actual output XML values, edited transform/name and stored Layout text. A separate source-field merge regression verifies that uppercase UUID aliases follow collision remaps for both field owners and Connection references, rather than losing a field or retargeting a relation.

Finding Save/export behavior
Equivalent supported normalization Normal canonical save/export; retain semantic values and provenance.
Valid retained standard field with modeled owner Validate and project into standard XML; normal save/export, no consent loop.
Missing authored GDTF or retained source resource Resource error; preserve target and dirty state; never replace an imported definition with a dummy.
Malformed retained XML, ambiguous reference or invalid identity Specific error; preserve target and dirty state.
Invalid destination, close or atomic replacement failure Archive IO error; preserve target; clean temporary file.
VideoScreen/Projector, media, parametric children, multipatch and standard Symbol topology Retain validated structure/resources around edited typed nodes; normal canonical save/export.
Nested Symdef graphs and edited instance geometry Typed nested instances, cycle/reference checks, isolated definition for an edited instance; retain original/unused definitions.
Model with available external textures/buffers Preserve original model bytes and relative resource tree in a stable package namespace.

The follow-up replaces the missing structural preservation owners with mvr_source_structure_capture/projection/edits/merge.cpp. The former importer flattened geometry for display and retained only neutral descriptors for media nodes. The ordinary writer consequently lacked their topology and payloads; preflight correctly refused loss. The new source evidence is immutable, scene-owned and reconstructed from canonical XML on reopen. Ordinary typed writers still own editable fields. This removes the listed representation blockers instead of suppressing diagnostics or maintaining an alternate PSTG scene. A recovery-copy consent path is unnecessary for these covered cases. For editable owners, structural validation covers the restored geometry and hierarchy; existing identifier/DMX/network validators remain authoritative, including published-standard cases that disagree with the pinned XSD (signed identifiers and IPv6). Source-only media payloads use their pinned standard type. Native editor range limits retain the existing bounded policy.

ProjectStructured*Roundtrip independently validates synthetic standard input, then imports it, edits existing Fixture name/transform, a nested Fixture, Truss placement and real Layout text. Six variants exercise basic structure, edited instance geometry, external textures, their combination and collision merge with/without textures. They inspect actual output node types, ownership, Symbol UUIDs/references, source-only Classing and a numeric identifier beyond the editor's int32 range, media and texture bytes. Both the standard Scene and its editable fields survive actual PSTG reopen and three saves. They compare all ordered embedded/standalone canonical ZIP entry payloads and unchanged source archive bytes. Explicit Direct Geometry3D compatibility remains a distinct output. Mixed direct geometry and multiple Symbols share one owner; editing one Symbol's geometry retains the other instance and original definitions.

Missing media/texture/GDTF (including an unrelated same-name file elsewhere), invalid source identities, cyclic references, malformed retained fields and invalid/write-failing targets retain separate failures, original target bytes, dirty state and no temporary-file leaks. These are bounded preservation and transaction checks, not certification of every provider extension or physical disk-exhaustion behavior.

Save As now changes current path/display name only after success; recent-file updates remain on that same success branch. Save preparation rolls back its state on failure. Archive publication closes its output and atomically replaces the destination, without a copy-overwrite fallback. All error diagnostics are available from the dialog's details control after the busy overlay closes. The UI boundary test checks ordering; the native UI test checks overlay lifetime on both failure and exception.

Focused Linux Debug commands:

cmake --build build/wsl-x64-debug --target project_preserved_fields_roundtrip_test mvr_symdef_preservation_test mvr_merge_analyzer_applier_test -j4
ctest --test-dir build/wsl-x64-debug -R '^(Project(PreservedFields|Structured.*)Roundtrip|MvrSymdefPreservation|MvrMergeAnalyzerApplier|MvrSourceStructureBoundary)$' --output-on-failure -j2
cmake --build build/wsl-x64-debug --target perastage_check_translations

The focused structural/resource suite passes 20/20 tests, including the independent Python Symdef/Focus/Class readers. The existing precision corpus checks 19 Trusses under nested groups, unedited numeric provenance, one-ULP translation, group movement, rotation/scale and repeated actual save/reload. Source projection leaves the ordinary writer's prepared local matrix untouched when its native owner and placement already match; it does not recompute and narrow unrelated authored values during a parent edit. The first affected resource remains available in the save-failure API alongside all detailed findings.

The native save UI lifetime check runs under Xvfb. Physical disk exhaustion and the Windows atomic replacement API have not been exercised here; Windows/macOS manual validation remains pending.

Legend parity

The production adapters now use the bundled PerastageSans metrics and the existing typography::Compose engine. The same logical frame produces the same name lines, row frames, header baselines, text-cell clips, symbol slots and column widths. Preview draws positioned glyph contours; PDF embeds the same font and retains selectable vector text. There are no Legend target profiles, platform font measurements or typography compensation factors. Event Table and free-text typography remain unchanged. Command-symbol stroke units are resolved before drawing and shared by both targets. Output paper scaling is one uniform fit after composition, preserving aspect ratio and the selected output page size/orientation.

At a 180 x 100 point frame, with three visible rows, all three enabled symbol views, Count and Ch columns, the actual adapters assert:

Fixture Reported original preview / PDF mismatch New preview and PDF nameLines
Exterior Linear-1200 Graze Exterior / Linear-1200 Graze versus Exterior Linear-1200 / Graze Exterior / Linear-1200 Graze
MAC Ultra Performance MAC Ultra / Performance versus one line MAC Ultra / Performance
Martin Atomic 3000 LED Martin Atomic / 3000 LED versus one line Martin Atomic / 3000 LED

The original screenshot's page/frame dimensions are unavailable, so this is a controlled reproduction with the exact names, not a reconstruction of its private layout. At 300 points wide all three names fit on one line on both targets. The two-line remainder stays in the plan; its cell clips visual overspill rather than painting into Ch. Font changes from accidental legacy platform/PDF choices are intentional; wrapping is now deterministic.

Production-adapter tests cover 0/1/3/5/20/100 rows, 120/180/300/600 point widths, preview zooms 50/80/100/200%, and PDF scales 0.5/1/2. They compare complete plan positions and inspect the actual PDF drawing stream's text/baseline commands. The PDF document test checks embedded font resources, vector paths for each view, all toggle combinations, counts, mixed page ordering and independence of a second Legend, Event Table, free text, view and image. pdftotext also extracts all three exact names from the 300-point production-exporter PDF.

UTF-8 diacritics and contiguous long names remain valid at every split. Unsupported UTF-8 remains in source data; the bounded WinAnsi repertoire omits unsupported glyphs consistently on both targets and reports line/byte/hex findings, capped at 16 details with an uncapped total count. PDF completion exposes those details. Full Unicode shaping/rendering is not claimed.

LayoutLegendRasterParity runs both production adapters, renders actual PDFs with Poppler and normalizes each page to four pixels per document point. It checks per-text-cell dark-ink bounding boxes within one raster pixel (0.25 pt), and mean absolute RGB error below 3/255, excluding the two-pixel page-edge crop. Independent plan/stream assertions require identical logical coordinates; raster tolerances cover antialiasing and font hinting, not layout differences. Results are identical across all three PDF output scales at each width:

Width (pt) Mean absolute RGB error (/255) Maximum ink bounds delta (px)
120 0.8178 0
180 2.1953 1
300 1.0379 1
600 0.7963 1

The generated preview PNGs and PDF rasters were also inspected. Reproduce and retain those review artifacts with:

python3 tests/check_legend_raster_parity.py --preview build/wsl-x64-debug/tests/layout_legend_preview_test --pdf build/wsl-x64-debug/tests/layout_legend_pdf_test --xvfb xvfb-run --pdftoppm pdftoppm --output /tmp/perastage-legend-evidence

This test uses only Python's standard library plus optional test tools Xvfb/Poppler; it adds no application dependency or font binary. It is registered on Linux when those tools are available. Native Windows/macOS visual validation and interactive Windows PDF-viewer zoom review remain pending.

Combined verification and merge gate

The Debug application builds and starts under Xvfb; the live CLI returns a successful scene.summary. All 79 selected CTest checks pass, including real MVR/PSTG round trips, source matrix precision, fixture-label override reconciliation, Layout image/resource and history regressions, MVR-xchange protocol, native save UI lifetime, production Legend adapters and raster parity. This is a focused suite, not a full repository/hosted-CI pass.

Review the project-save corrections independently from Legend composition. The covered P0 structures have a normal canonical save/reopen/export route; B1 retains its Linux automated parity gate. Keep PR 2501 open as a draft while platform validation/review is pending; do not merge automatically. Neither these tests nor the source-preservation service certify arbitrary future MVR versions, provider extensions or unavailable external resources.

Recoverable MVR 1.5 anomalies: baseline and correction

At fdd8df84, a synthetic 1.5 package with three repeated-UUID SceneObjects, distinct placements, one shared GLB, a valid Class target and two empty Truss GDTFSpec/GDTFMode pairs reproduces the reported blockers. All three editable objects survive import. Retained topology still contains the repeated raw identity; structural projection does not reconcile it. Preflight reports Duplicate source node identity, owner-ambiguous Classing and two Table 28 mode errors. PSTG save and standalone canonical export both fail; prior target and imported source bytes remain intact.

The positive regression is now MvrImportAnomalyRoundtrip. Import caches the existing resolver result per XML node and applies it to the private XML working copy before Classing and source topology are captured. This removes the two inconsistent identity views. mvr_source_recovery.cpp also reconciles retained metadata from an earlier imported session on an export-only clone. Its fallback requires a unique actual object with matching layer/local numeric provenance; it never allocates a second editable identity or rewrites a model filename. The scanner now distinguishes substantive GDTFSpec from empty XML whitespace.

The native-reader/writer regression and seven variants cover absent, empty, whitespace-only, valid, missing-mode and empty-mode bindings, dependent Network assignments and 1.6 input. They edit a Fixture, move one formerly duplicated object and edit Layout text; save/reopen/save succeeds. Every ordered embedded scene.mvr entry/payload matches standalone canonical output. Three objects and Class targets survive, the one GLB keeps its exact bytes and original basename (which deliberately contains the old UUID), output identities are unique, and the imported ZIP remains unchanged. The standard scene is independently validated against the pinned official 1.6 XSD using the same documented root UserData qualification as the earlier tests. The earlier-session test verifies exactly two owner identity warnings and no live-provenance mutation. Missing optional modes produce precise DataOmitted warnings; dependent Network values are disclosed while DMX addresses remain. Complete authored bindings survive.

Reproduction commands (Linux Debug):

cmake --build build/wsl-x64-debug --target project_preserved_fields_roundtrip_test mvr_standard_preservation_test mvr_export_preparation_test -j4
ctest --test-dir build/wsl-x64-debug -R '^(MvrImportAnomaly.*|MvrStandardPreservation|MvrExportPreparation)$' --output-on-failure -j2

Result: 10/10 passed, including eight native archive round trips. The combined focused regression selection subsequently passed 87/87 under Xvfb, including Legend vector/raster parity, source/Symdef/Class/Focus, numeric and DMX preservation, MVR-xchange, project IO and save UI. The Debug application and perastage_check_translations build successfully; mandatory guards and generated-document drift checks pass. This fixes the synthetic reproduction of the reported duplicate-owner/empty-binding blockers; it does not prove the unavailable private package passes. No private source archive, filename or object name is present in these fixtures/docs.

Best-effort canonical publication follow-up

The former preflight treated every durable preservation finding as a veto before trying repair. mvr_export_preparation.cpp::Prepare now repairs a private snapshot before running the unchanged strict validators on its actual projection. PSTG, ordinary canonical MVR and MVR-xchange keep one serializer and effective options. No alternate native scene or unchecked ignore-errors option is introduced.

Additional causes found and corrected:

  • mvr_identifier_preservation.cpp narrowed legal XML integers to int32. Valid wide scalars now retain lexical values, independently of their editor projection.
  • Native ownership, nonfinite components and legacy primary-address conflicts could veto unrelated scene edits. Repair is component/relationship specific; an explicit primary edit keeps secondary breaks.
  • Source and Symbol identities used different occurrence views. The reader's occurrence plan now also identifies genuinely ambiguous external relationships; older retained sessions reuse the same audit with their actual recovered IDs. Class targets remain independent of owner identity. No model filename is rewritten from UUID substrings.
  • Resource failures during merge could leave a reference matching an unrelated target namesake. Exact owner/resource failure evidence forces omission or an explicit required-profile substitution before packaging; a basename is not proof of source ownership. Other available geometry and resources remain.
  • GDTF canonicalization rejected unsupported FixtureType payloads after initial import. An explicit MVR-only projection removes just those attributes/subtrees with complete escaped evidence, then validates the derivative. Truss bindings accept only an issued path/source/output SHA-256 proof and verified mode/wires.
  • Truss type and planning-power edits could disappear on reopen. Versioned existing application metadata now retains those values and explicit zero/empty overrides without inventing a standard GDTF write owner.
  • Generated revision and nested ZIP timestamps changed GDTF payload bytes across saves. Canonical publication keeps authored dates and omits only generated optional dates; generated ZIP metadata is deterministic.
  • Standalone export truncated its destination before all resources were copied. The standalone archive-publication change closes a complete temporary archive before atomic replacement. Nested GDTF writers now check write/close failures too.
Finding Save/export decision
Equivalent normalization Normal success; retained semantics
Deterministic identity/component repair Success with precise repair finding; live scene unchanged
Invalid/unresolved relationship, unavailable optional resource Omit only affected payload/reference; Warning/DataOmitted
Unusable required fixture profile Use the supplied installed fallback and actual declared mode; Warning/DataSubstituted
No safe physical GDTF write target Keep standard source definition and explicit native planning value; RequestNotHonored warning
Source acquisition failed despite a target namesake Never borrow that file; project only independently available content
Actual IO, serializer or generated-output invalidity Real failure; previous bytes/dirty/session path retained

Material findings include type, UUID/occurrence, field/path, action and original content. They are retained as inert permitted UserData evidence and logged on reopen; no automatic reconciliation executes that evidence. Missing binary assets require the original package or an explicit rebind/reimport. Ordinary Save has no consent loop; warnings are logged, and MVR export exposes grouped, expandable details. Failed saves still close the busy overlay before dialogs.

The native corpus includes 34 publication cases plus the earlier eight synthetic 1.5/1.6 import variants. It checks real save/reopen/save/export, edited Fixtures, repeated-ID object placement, Layout text, Classing, Symbols, model dependencies, wide integers and native planning metadata. Ordered scene.mvr entries and payload bytes equal standalone output; two derivative cases cross a ZIP clock tick deliberately. The source package remains byte-identical. Acquisition-loss assertions inspect the actual affected definition, not just a successful boolean.

The standard Scene is checked against the unchanged pinned 1.6 XSD. Existing UserData content and published syntax/XSD discrepancies (signed identifiers and breaks, Universe.Address, IPv6) are explicitly qualified in the legacy corpus; full-document pinned-XSD conformance is not claimed. The private production MVR was unavailable, so synthetic evidence does not certify that file.

Local Linux Debug qualification: 128/128 passed under Xvfb in the combined MVR/project/Legend regression selection. The application and perastage_check_translations build. Module-tree, GUI dependency, source-size, repository-hygiene and MVR service boundary guards pass. Documentation has no drift.
